activation_fixture.format: 44 consecutive little-endian BF16 final-norm vectors, step-major, 5120 elements and 10240 bytes per step

capture_method.mechanism: ordinary gdb breakpoint on ReferenceRunner::last_trace after the completed trace D2H copy; dump only the final-norm slice from the pinned host trace buffer
capture_method.command_shape: qwen3x-orin generate MODEL_DIR --prompt <pinned Chinese CUDA prompt> --max-tokens 26 --trace --prefill-chunk-size 32 --projection-backend sm87

native_trace_validation.result: raw slices match the hashes emitted by the same native run

production_lm_head.argmax_tie_policy: strict greater-than scan over ascending token ids; the smallest token id wins a BF16 tie
production_lm_head.nonfinite_policy: a nonfinite logits result is an error

offline_screen.weight_decode: E2M1 codebook times E4M3FN block scale; positive tensor weight_scale_2 is applied after the row dot product
offline_screen.accumulation_caveat: Torch GEMM does not reproduce the production lane accumulator and warp-reduction order. Matching BF16 argmax is a sanity check, not a bit-exact candidate correctness result. Any implementation must use the directed-round proof contract below and then pass native exact gates.

admission_gate.same_argmax_requirement: provably identical BF16 argmax on every frozen P19-P43 activation
admission_gate.traffic_accounting: count prefix weight and scale reads, survivor weight and scale reads, and all bound sidecar reads; do not credit cache reuse that has not been measured

fixed_cut_two_kernel.reason: The best scanned cut cannot save 55 MB even under the optimistic logical-payload model and even if sidecar traffic is made free.

algorithm.pass_1: read one common prefix for every row and compute a partial dot P_i
algorithm.global_lower_bound: L = max_i(P_i - H_i), with the production-rounding envelope included by a real implementation
algorithm.survivor_rule: row i survives when P_i + H_i >= L; equality survives conservatively
algorithm.pass_2: fully recompute every survivor with the exact production BF16 LM-head path and run the production tie-aware argmax
algorithm.continuation_state: none; the prefix is deliberately recomputed for every survivor

sidecar.l2_note: The sidecar is below the device maximum persisting-L2 capacity but above the observed current persisting limit. The rejection remains unchanged even when its traffic cost is forced to zero.

scan.selection_objective: maximum mean saved bytes; the same cut also maximizes worst-step saved bytes

q20_single_kernel_progressive.reason_for_retention: The zero-code logical-traffic screen clears 55 MB on all 25 frozen steps, but only under implementation and scheduling assumptions that have not been validated.

design.execution: keep the production partial accumulators in registers and stop future row reads after a proof succeeds
design.separate_continuation_state_rejection: Four FP32 accumulators per lane for 32 lanes require 512 bytes per row, or 127139840 bytes over 248320 rows before counting both a write and a read.
design.required_predication_granularity: individual row, not one continue decision for the whole four-row quad
design.required_incumbent_publication: a deterministic completed-wave publication barrier or a stronger mechanism that makes the simulated prior-wave incumbent available before the next wave

sidecar.traffic_accounting: charge all 19 values for every row even though an implementation could avoid later sidecar reads after a row exits

traffic_formula.f: total row-block weight and scale reads divided by 248320*20

simulation.incumbent: for each 2048-row wave after the first, use the largest BF16-rounded offline row score from all completed earlier waves; the first wave runs fully
simulation.bound: one global Cauchy suffix bound at each 256-column checkpoint

incumbent_sensitivity.meaning: conservative screening sensitivity roughly equal to one BF16 ULP in the observed top-logit region; not a substitute for the directed-round proof
large robustness sensitivity only; not an estimated production rounding error

p2_entry_conditions: build an offline FP64-to-upward-FP32 suffix-norm sidecar and validate every stored norm against an independent checker
implement a test-only kernel without changing the production route
retain partial accumulators only in registers inside one kernel; do not materialize the 127139840-byte continuation state
prove per-row predication actually suppresses future weight and scale transactions rather than only suppressing arithmetic
provide deterministic incumbent publication or directly measure and close the asynchronous schedule against the traffic gate
pass exact BF16 token-id and tie-policy gates on every frozen activation before any timing claim
measure sidecar, weight, and scale traffic with NCU and require at least 55000000 average bytes saved per call after all added traffic
query registers, local memory, shared memory, and active CTAs per SM; reject spills or occupancy loss that erase the benefit
run same-binary B-C-C-B P19/C32/max26 Decode timing and require no regression on any mirrored round
keep full-statistics and all unsupported shapes on the exact current fallback

exactness_contract_for_any_future_candid.weight_coefficients: Decode the exact checkpoint E2M1 and E4M3FN values; do not replace them with a learned or lossy approximation.
exactness_contract_for_any_future_candid.sidecar_construction: Compute each norm in FP64 or wider, then round upward to a finite FP32 value. Overflow or nonfinite metadata makes the row ineligible for pruning.
exactness_contract_for_any_future_candid.activation_norm: Accumulate BF16-square sums with a directed-upward procedure and round sqrt upward, or provide an independently proven equivalent.
exactness_contract_for_any_future_candid.partial_error_envelope: A proof may bound the partial and final FP32 paths with gamma_48 times an upward bound on sum(abs(w*x)); the final weight_scale_2 multiplication must also be rounded outward.
exactness_contract_for_any_future_candid.bf16_rounding: Convert the upper endpoint monotonically and conservatively across the BF16 RNE boundary. A universal strict-upper-below-incumbent rule is acceptable and intentionally conservative.
exactness_contract_for_any_future_candid.tie_and_index: If using an index-sensitive comparison, a row with a smaller id than the incumbent must be proven strictly below it; a larger id may be proven less-than-or-equal. Otherwise retain all equality cases and let the exact fallback resolve them.
exactness_contract_for_any_future_candid.nonfinite: Any nonfinite activation, partial, bound, scale, or output disables pruning for the affected call or row and preserves the production error/fallback behavior.
exactness_contract_for_any_future_candid.final_selection: Every survivor must be evaluated by the exact production-order BF16 path, and final argmax must preserve the smallest-id tie policy.

claim_limits: The raw final-norm fixture is external under /tmp and is identified by size and SHA256; it is not durable repository evidence by itself.
Trace mode disables the Decode Graph cache. These are exact native serial-path activations; raw BF16 identity of Graph-replayed hidden state was not separately captured in this audit.
The fixture covers one tokenizer-pinned prompt and P19-P43 only. It does not establish traffic savings for other prompts, positions, context lengths, model revisions, or sampling modes.
The offline Torch reduction order differs from the production CUDA reduction order. The screen can reject a structurally weak design, but it cannot certify a future kernel's bit-exact result.

The fixed-cut result is an optimistic logical-payload calculation. It excludes launch, reduction, argmax, activation, output, atomic, synchronization, and instruction overhead; those omissions can only strengthen its rejection.
The q20 result is a simulation, not an implementation, NCU measurement, Nsys measurement, latency benchmark, CUDA Graph validation, resource result, or production performance claim.
The q20 simulation assumes per-row traffic suppression and completed 2048-row wave incumbent publication. An asynchronous production schedule may read more bytes and fail the gate.
The q20 sidecar is charged in full, but cache residency is neither assumed nor measured. Conversely, cache-line overfetch and transaction inefficiency are not modeled.
No register count, spill behavior, occupancy, barrier cost, atomic contention, divergence cost, or BF16-bound instruction cost is known for q20.
The -0.125 and -1.0 incumbent perturbations are sensitivity screens, not formal floating-point error bounds.
Full-statistics logits are not eligible for pruning under this record and must remain on the current exact route.
MTP is excluded from the design, data, and claims in this artifact.
No README, ROADMAP, PERFORMANCE_BASELINE, source, test, build, or production-policy update is authorized by this metadata alone.
